records.material: Polyethylene (PE), including linear low-density and high-density grades
records.reported_effect: An industry report said PRefChem shut downstream polymer units in the week ended 7 February, taking 750,000 tonnes per year of PE nameplate capacity offline, with market sources anticipating at least one to two months offline. It also reported reduced regional availability alongside weak demand and existing oversupply.

source.publisher: Modern Plastics Network, reporting market sources and ICIS data
source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The 750,000 tonnes per year is nameplate capacity, not measured lost production or an unfilled quantity. The anticipated one-to-two-month outage was a market-source estimate, not a verified recovery date.
The report also describes weak demand and market oversupply; reduced capacity does not establish a general market shortage or an affected customer's order.
The listed products include plastic articles, but the resin grade and composition of any case-study product and any supplier or shipment relationship are unverified.
The exact shutdown and restart dates and the reported cause are not established in the reviewed source.

search_window.note: The reported shutdown week ended 7 February; the retrieval range starts at the beginning of that week and extends 14 days after the 10 March report. It does not establish a continuous outage or restart date.

records.material: Rare-earth materials used in automotive components
records.reported_effect: CBS reported on 13 June that Ford's CEO attributed a temporary factory shutdown in the preceding month to a rare-earth shortage and described supply as day-to-day. The report links the supply difficulty to China's export licensing process.

source.publisher: CBS News, reporting a Bloomberg TV interview
source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The report does not name the shut factory or give precise shutdown dates, its location, duration, the exact material specification, or a recovery date; a US factory is not independently established.
The United States is the reported downstream supply context, not a verified location of the unnamed factory. Ford is the reporting manufacturer, not a verified material supplier.
The supplied list includes motorized appliances and vehicle parts; no corresponding case-study component composition, supplier, production impact, or shipment has been verified.
The report attributes a shortage and factory shutdown to Ford's CEO; the relationship to the Chinese control is contextual and does not establish the exact controlled item or licence decision.

search_window.note: The source describes a shutdown in May and continuing concerns in its 13 June report; this retrieval window includes May and 14 days after the report, not a verified continuous shortage or shutdown.

records.material: Nexperia semiconductors used in automotive control systems
records.reported_effect: Taipei Times reported that an October supply disruption and blocked exports from Nexperia's Chinese factories contributed to component shortages and production slowdowns among automotive manufacturers. Its 17 November report said some deliveries were reported to have restarted.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: China identifies the location of the reported supply disruption, not the location of the downstream automotive production cuts.
The report does not establish exact disruption start and end dates, affected part numbers, or the extent and continuity of resumed deliveries.
The supplied products include electrical controls and vehicle parts, but no case-study product, supplier, part number, or shipment has been matched to Nexperia.
The article is a secondary account; the manufacturer's original statement at https://www.nexperia.com/about/news-events/press-releases/update-on-company-developments-2 was inaccessible during review.

search_window.note: The report describes an October disruption and reported subsequent deliveries; the window expands October and extends 14 days beyond the 17 November report for retrieval, not as verified continuous shortage.

records.reported_effect: Reuters reported on 10 March that Formosa Petrochemical declared force majeure on some supplies, including ethylene and propylene, because Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions delayed feedstock deliveries. Its spokesperson said two crackers were operating at about 70 percent.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The source describes a notice covering some supplies, not a complete shutdown or a quantified shortfall for all customers; the potential further cracker shutdown was conditional.
Ethylene and propylene are feedstocks for plastics, not proof that the listed plastic products contain a specific polymer or depend on this facility.
No case-study supplier, transaction, shortage quantity, actual delivery failure, or incident end has been verified.
The linked geopolitical record is related conflict context and a separate Singapore fuel effect, not proof of the same product shortage.

search_window.note: Fourteen days either side of the report date for retrieval only; the precise start and end of the supply constraint are not established.

records.reported_effect: Malay Mail, citing industry accounts, reported PET resin shortages affecting Malaysian packaging and that dairy producer Farm Fresh temporarily shifted toward carton-based and alternative packaging.

source.publisher: Malay Mail, citing Utusan Malaysia and industry accounts
source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: The report primarily concerns bottles and food packaging; listed plastic and packaging categories are contextual and are not confirmed to use PET.
No case-study supplier, purchase, shortage quantity, shipment, or product effect is identified.
The reported packaging substitution is an observed response, not an end date for the shortage. The onset and end remain unknown.
The linked geopolitical record concerns the broader conflict and a separate Singapore fuel effect; it is not evidence that the same firm or supply was affected.

search_window.note: Fourteen days either side of the report date for retrieval only; the precise start and end of the supply constraint are not established.
